question.worked_solution:
Since $\frac{2y}{6y+1}+Z=\frac{x+1}{3x},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Z & =\frac{x+1}{3x}-\frac{2y}{6y+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to put the fractions over a common denominator of $3x(6y+1),$ since there are no common factors in either denominator that we can exploit. 

To do this, we multiply the top and bottom of the first fraction by $6y+1,$ and the top and bottom of the second fraction by $3x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}Z & =\frac{x+1}{3x}-\frac{2y}{6y+1} \\  & =\frac{6y+1}{6y+1}\cdot \frac{x+1}{3x}-\frac{3x}{3x}\cdot \frac{2y}{6y+1} \\  & =\frac{(6y+1)(x+1)}{3x(6y+1)}-\frac{3x(2y)}{3x(6y+1)} \\  & =\frac{(6y+1)(x+1)-3x(2y)}{3x(6y+1)} \\  & =\frac{6yx+x+6y+1-6xy}{3x(6y+1)} \\  & =\frac{x+6y+1}{3x(6y+1)}\end{aligned}
$$
